title: ProofV6
description: Proof as a planner rather than only a checker. v5 verifies claims after they are atomized; v6 derives, before release, what WOULD have to be proved — so that a gate evaluates a declared obligation set instead of running a hard-coded list of checks hidden inside a command. Three rules hold throughout and none of them bends. UNAVAILABLE IS NOT PASSING: a check that could not run is recorded as not run, with its reason, and never absorbed into a pass rate. AN ABSENT CHECK IS NOT A PASSING CHECK: an obligation nothing evaluated is open, not satisfied. AND NOTHING PROMOTES A RELIABILITY TYPE: a judged result never becomes verified because a provider was confident, because two providers agreed, or because a threshold was met — constraint C005 refuses it and there is no configuration that changes this. This document is a DEFINITION LIBRARY: validate against a named member of `$defs`, never against the document root.

ProofObligation.description: Something that must be established before a subject may be released. Derived from typed state, a release target and a policy — not written by hand — so that `what must be proved?` is answerable before any work begins and identical for two people asking the same question of the same graph.

obligation_id.description: Identity of the obligation, derived from its subject, kind and policy source so that regenerating obligations for an unchanged graph produces the same set rather than a fresh one. Without that, no obligation could carry a status across a re-plan.

subject.description: What must be established about. Pinned to a state when the obligation has been discharged, because a result proves something about the state it examined and about nothing else.

kind.description: What must be established. The field that makes an obligation set readable: a claim requiring anchor integrity, numeric value and citation resolution has three obligations rather than one vague requirement to be checked.

required_basis.description: The reliability types that would satisfy this obligation. Minimum one, and stated as a SET because policy differs by target: an internal memo may accept a judged entailment where a regulatory filing accepts only a verified one, and the same claim then carries different obligations for different outputs. This is where a policy's strictness actually lives.

required_checks.description: Specific check identifiers that must run. Empty means any check producing an acceptable basis will do; naming them is how a policy pins a particular method rather than an outcome.

policy_source.description: The exact policy state this obligation was derived from. Required, and it is why constraint C019 puts the policy inside the proof closure: a rule that changed six months later must not retroactively alter what `passed` meant for an older release.

status.description: Where the obligation stands. Derived from the results bound to it rather than set, so it cannot be marked satisfied by anything but evidence.

satisfied_by.description: The verification results or judgment records that discharge it. Plural, because some obligations need several; and carried by digest so that a result later found to have examined the wrong state can be traced to everything it was counted toward.

waiver.description: The record of a deliberate release with this obligation open, where policy permits one. Present so a waived obligation stays visible as waived — an obligation that could be deleted would let a release look complete when what happened is that somebody accepted a risk.

release_targets.description: Which targets require this. An obligation binding for one output and not another is the ordinary case, and a set that flattened them would either over-constrain the memo or under-constrain the filing.

state_digest.description: Digest over the canonical obligation state, so a release closure binds the obligations as they stood at build.

ProofObligationKind.description: What kind of thing must be established. Closed, because a gate evaluates a declared set and an open vocabulary would let an obligation be declared that no check knows how to discharge — which reads on a report as permanently open rather than as a mistake. Not every kind applies to every subject; the planner decides applicability from typed state, which is why a claim with no quantity generates no numeric obligation instead of generating one that trivially passes.

oneOf.description: The evidence anchor resolves and the anchored bytes are what they were. The obligation everything else rests on: a claim whose anchor has drifted is unsupported however well it verifies against the drifted text.
Quoted text matches the source exactly. Distinct from anchor integrity because a correct anchor can still be quoted inaccurately.
The stated quantity is what the source states.
The unit is the source's unit, or a correct conversion of it.
Compared quantities share a dimension. What constraint C013 enforces, and what stops a rate being compared with a count.
A stated range or interval is the source's.
A rate's base population is stated and is the source's. The obligation that stops `43%` travelling without the thing it is 43% of.
A stated instant is the source's.
A stated period is the source's.
A named entity appears in the source as the claim says it does.
A citation resolves to a retrievable source. Distinguished from anchor integrity because a citation can be well formed, resolvable and about something else entirely.
The claim's territory is the source's.
The claim's population is the source's. The scope failure that most often survives review, because both statements read as true.
The claim's period is the source's.
A claim did not become more certain than its source. The obligation that catches `may` becoming `will` in a rewrite that changed nothing else.
A negation survived rewriting. Rarely violated and catastrophic when it is.
Who said it survived rewriting. What stops a source's reported claim being rendered as the author's own.
A term is used under the definition that governs it. What makes a definition change propagate rather than sit inert.
A declared exception survived rendering. The obligation with the largest legal consequence per instance: an obligation rendered without its exception clause states a duty nobody agreed to.
A claim's epistemic realm survived rendering. Constraint C011, and what stops a scenario figure reading as a measurement.

A paraphrase is entailed by its source where no exact support exists. THE OBLIGATION MOST OFTEN DISCHARGED BY JUDGMENT rather than verification, which is why `required_basis` is per-obligation: a policy may accept a judged entailment for one target and require exact support for another.
A forecast names its assumptions and baseline. What stops a projection circulating as a finding.
An argument's cited premises exist and carry their own proof states. All the system can check about reasoning, and it checks it.
An actor held the capability they exercised, at the time they exercised it. Constraint C020.
A decision's target had not moved when it was taken. Constraints C006 and C007.
The approved bytes are the shipped bytes. Constraint C010.
Every dependency the release claims is present in its closure. Constraint C009.

ObligationStatus.description: Where an obligation stands. FIVE VALUES, AND THE MIDDLE THREE ARE THE POINT: `open`, `unavailable` and `undeterminable` all mean the obligation is not discharged, and they send a person to three different places — do the work, fix the installation, accept that it cannot be settled from here. A schema with `satisfied` and `failed` alone would force all three into `failed`, and a gate report full of failures nobody can act on is one whose failures stop being read.

oneOf.description: Not yet evaluated. The honest default, and where every obligation starts.
Discharged by results whose basis is in `required_basis`. Requires the results to exist and to name this subject state; nothing else produces this value.
Evaluated and not met. A finding, and the only one of the five that says something is wrong with the work.

A required check could not run — no provider on this surface, an offline verifier profile, a dependency out of reach. NEVER counted as passing and never counted as failing: the subject may be perfectly sound and nobody has been able to tell. A release declaring this is stating an omission, which is stronger than a missing field.

Evaluated, and the answer cannot be reached from the available evidence — a source that neither supports nor contradicts the claim. Kept apart from `failed` because the repairs differ entirely: one is to correct the claim and the other is to find better support.

BasisKind.description: The reliability types, named as bare kinds so a policy can require one without supplying its payload. THE SET IS CLOSED AND ORDERED BY NOTHING. There is no `Confident`. There is no `AI Verified`. There is no `94.7% True`. A policy requiring `Verified` is not requiring a higher score, it is requiring a different KIND of thing, and no accumulation of judgment ever becomes one.

oneOf.description: Established by a deterministic check that anyone can re-run to the same answer. Constraint C004 requires a deterministic engine to have produced it.
Established by a measurement carrying its numerator, denominator and population. Not a weaker verification: a different claim, about a sample.

Assessed by a named provider. Carries the provider's identity because the assessment is theirs and inherits none of the system's standing. Constraint C005 forbids typing it Verified under any circumstance.
Asserted by a named person with standing. The honest basis for a great deal of legitimate content, and it must never be rendered as though a machine had checked it.

VerificationResult.description: What one check found about one exact state. `check_version` is required alongside `check`, because a check is software: an improved implementation that finds something its predecessor missed has not proved the old result wrong, it has produced a different result, and a record that could not tell them apart could never explain why something that passed in March fails in July.

check_version.description: Which version of it. Load-bearing for reproducibility: a release closure binds check versions, so re-verifying an old release runs the checks that actually judged it rather than today's.

subject_state.description: THE EXACT STATE EXAMINED. The field that makes staleness computable: when the subject's digest moves, this result demonstrably describes something else, and no wall-clock heuristic is needed to notice.

dependencies.description: Every other state the result relied on — the anchor, the source version, the governing definition, the policy. What makes invalidation precise rather than approximate: a definition changing invalidates exactly the results that read it.

basis.description: The reliability type this result carries. A deterministic engine emits Verified and cannot emit anything else; a judgment provider emits Judged and cannot emit Verified. The constraint engine enforces both, because the alternative is a configuration flag that would eventually be set.

detail.description: What was found, in words a person can act on. Most valuable on a failure, where `expected 11,800 from the source and the claim states 12,400` is a repair and `numeric.value failed` is a search.

engine.description: Which implementation produced it. Required in a dual-core window, where Python and Rust must agree byte for byte and any divergence has to be attributable to one of them.

state_digest.description: Digest over the canonical result, so a closure binds the result as it was recorded.

CheckOutcome.description: What a check found. `not_run` is a legitimate outcome recorded as a result rather than as an absence, because absence is invisible: a subject with no result and a subject whose check could not run look identical to a gate, and only one of them is a finding a release must declare.

oneOf.description: The property holds for the examined state.
The property does not hold. A finding about the work.
The check does not apply — a numeric check on a claim with no quantity. Recorded so a report can distinguish a check that had nothing to do from one that was skipped.

The check could not run, with the reason in `detail`. NEVER absorbed into a pass rate: a run of 40 checks with 38 passes and 2 not-run is not 95%, it is 38 answers and 2 unknowns, and the second number is the one worth reading.

The check ran and failed to complete. Distinct from `fail`, which is a finding about the subject; this is a finding about the check, and confusing them sends somebody to correct a claim that was never examined.

EngineIdentity.description: Which implementation produced a result. Present because the migration plan runs two cores side by side for at least one release cycle, and the requirement is byte-identical output on shared fixtures. A result that could not say which core produced it makes that requirement unverifiable, and the operator asking `which core answered?` is entitled to a straight answer rather than an inference.

implementation.description: The engine. There is no silent fallback between implementations: a run that fell back has produced a result from a different engine and says so here.

binary_digest.description: Digest of the binary, where the deployment can produce one. What turns `version 6.0.1` from a label into a fact.

JudgmentRecord.description: What a named provider assessed about an exact state. A record of an opinion and never of a fact, which is why the provider's identity is required and why constraint C008 gives providers NO authority grants at all: a provider may assess and may never decide, approve, commit or sign, and an assessment arriving as though it were a check is the confusion the whole reliability model exists to prevent.

provider.description: Who assessed. Required and never anonymized: an assessment whose provider is unknown cannot be weighed, re-requested or held to a policy, and it is the provider's opinion rather than the system's finding.

obligation.description: The obligation this was requested against, where it was requested for one. Present so an unsolicited assessment is distinguishable from one a policy asked for.

rationale.description: The provider's reasoning, retained verbatim. A judgment a person cannot inspect is a judgment they have to take on trust, which is exactly what a Judged basis is meant to avoid asking of anybody.

responded_at.description: When it came back. Absent means outstanding, and an outstanding request is not a negative answer.

disagreement.description: How this assessment stands against others of the same subject. Recorded because two providers disagreeing is information, and a policy for a regulated target may require the disagreement be resolved before release rather than averaged away.

prompt_digest.description: Digest of exactly what the provider was asked. What makes an assessment re-requestable on the same terms, and what stops a differently-worded request being compared with an earlier answer as though the question had not changed.

ProviderRef.description: A judgment provider. Named as a first-class reference so that an assessment carries who made it into every rendering — the provider is replaceable and the policy is durable, and an assessment that lost its provider would have inherited the system's voice.

model.description: The specific model or panel, where the provider exposes one. Recorded because a provider's answer is a function of it, and comparing answers across a silent model change compares two different things.

JudgmentAssessment.description: What a provider found. `abstained` and `undeterminable` are both here and are not the same: one is the provider declining, and one is the provider answering that the question cannot be settled on the evidence given. Collapsing them loses the difference between a provider that is unavailable and a subject that is genuinely unresolvable.

oneOf.description: The provider assesses the subject as supported. Judged, and it stays Judged.
The provider assesses it as unsupported.
The provider finds the source contradicts the subject. Stronger than unsupported and worth its own value, since the repairs differ.
The provider cannot settle it on the evidence provided. An answer, and often the correct one.
The provider declined — policy, safety, or a subject outside its scope. Recorded so that a declined request is not read as a negative finding.

JudgmentDisagreement.description: How assessments of one subject stand against each other. NEVER AVERAGED INTO A SCORE. Two providers disagreeing about whether a paraphrase is entailed is a finding that belongs in front of a person, and a mean would erase precisely the signal that made it worth asking twice.

resolution.description: The decision that settled it, where policy required settlement. Absent means unresolved, and a policy for a regulated target may refuse release on exactly that.

policy_treatment.description: What the governing policy does about it. Recorded on the record so a reader can see that a disagreement was permitted rather than missed.

DisagreementStatus.description: Whether providers agree. `unknown` is present because a single assessment establishes nothing about agreement, and reporting it as `none` would claim a consensus of one.

oneOf.description: Several assessments and they agree.
Assessments disagree, and the disagreement is unsettled.
Disagreed and settled by an authorized decision.
Only one assessment exists, so agreement has not been tested. Never rendered as agreement.

DisagreementTreatment.description: How policy handles a judgment disagreement for a given target. Per-policy rather than global, because the right answer for an internal draft and for a regulatory filing are genuinely different — and the difference should live in the policy where it can be read, not in a reviewer's habits.

oneOf.description: Recorded and does not block. Appropriate where the judgment was optional to begin with.

Must be resolved before release. The correct treatment for a regulated target, where an unresolved disagreement about an entailment is an unresolved question about whether the document says something true.
Requires a decision by a named role rather than by whoever is releasing. For subjects where the disagreement itself indicates the matter needs somebody with standing.

ObligationWaiver.description: A deliberate release with an obligation open. Requires a decision digest rather than a flag, because waiving a proof obligation is an exercise of authority and recording it any other way creates a second approval path around the one the authority model governs. The obligation stays OPEN and waived; it is never marked satisfied, because it was not.

decision.description: The decision that waived it, carrying its own authority receipt.

reason.description: Why. Non-empty and rendered wherever the waiver is: a waiver whose reason is not shown to a reader of the released artifact is an undisclosed risk, and disclosure is the whole reason a waiver is a first-class object.

expires_at.description: When the waiver lapses. Absent means it holds for this release only rather than indefinitely — a waiver that silently carried into every future release would turn one accepted risk into a permanent exemption.

Invalidation.description: The record that something a proof depended on moved. Invalidation is DERIVED from digests rather than declared: when a state a result depended on changes, that result demonstrably describes a state that no longer exists, and the system knows it without anybody remembering. This is what makes verification stop expiring silently — the failure v5 was built to end and v6 inherits without weakening.

invalidation_id.description: Durable identity, so an invalidation raised and later repaired is one object with a history.

subject.description: What became invalid — a verification result, a judgment record, a decision, an argument.

cause.description: The state change that caused it. Named, because `this result is stale` sends nobody anywhere and `this result is stale because the definition it read was revised` sends them to the definition.

kind.description: What kind of dependency moved. Decides the repair, and the repairs are not comparable in cost.

severity.description: Whether the subject is definitely wrong or merely unverified. The distinction that stops every dependency change reading as an error, which is what makes an invalidation report worth opening.

detected_at.description: When it was detected — which is when the dependency moved, not when somebody noticed.

resolved_by.description: The new result or decision that repaired it. Absent means outstanding, and an outstanding invalidation is what makes a node stale — a flag nobody can clear by hand.

InvalidationKind.description: What moved underneath a proof. Enumerated because each leads to a different repair and a different cost, and a single `stale` marker would send a re-run and a re-approval to the same queue at the same apparent price.

oneOf.description: The examined subject itself changed. The commonest kind, usually repaired by re-running the check.
Something the result relied on changed — an anchor, a governing definition, a linked assumption. The subject may be untouched and the result is still about a world that has moved.
The underlying source has a new version. May require re-anchoring rather than re-checking, and constraint C003 requires an anchor into a superseded version to be explicit.
The check was updated. Does not make the old result wrong; it makes it a result from a previous implementation, and whether that still counts is a policy question.
The governing policy moved, so the obligation set itself may differ. Invalidates the QUESTION rather than the answer, which is why it is its own kind.
A grant relied on was revoked or expired. Constraint C020, and it reaches decisions rather than checks — the most expensive kind to repair, because the repair is somebody's attention.
A judgment provider is no longer accepted under policy. Its assessments do not become false; they stop being admissible, which is a distinction a report must preserve.

InvalidationSeverity.description: How badly a subject is damaged. Three values because collapsing them makes every dependency change look like an error, and a system that cries wolf on a whitespace change in an upstream source teaches its users to clear invalidations without reading them.

oneOf.description: The new state actively contradicts what the subject asserted. Definitely wrong, and it is a finding rather than a chore.
The subject may still hold and is no longer proved. The commonest severity, and the honest description of most staleness: nobody knows, and finding out is a re-run.

A dependency changed in a way that does not bear on the subject — a source revision that did not touch the anchored region. Recorded for the audit trail and does not make the subject stale, because marking it stale would spend a person's attention on nothing.
